stemMd: Which general principle best fits the author's analysis?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Information has value only in court.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Evaluate a rule partly by the behavior it induces under realistic conditions of information and attention.

options.label: C
options.textMd: A rule is optimal whenever it has a simple label.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A majority preference is irrelevant to every default.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Any penalty necessarily produces useful disclosure.

explanationMd: The author repeatedly asks how actual parties respond before opting out. The rule's nominal purpose is insufficient; information, comprehension, and feasible responses determine whether that purpose is realized.

distractorRationale.c: The label does not establish behavioral effects.
distractorRationale.e: Obscurity can prevent the intended response.
